blocker.summary: The r399-r431 chain is CLOSED (allocator, shutdown hang, presentation mechanism all fixed/live-verified). r432 fixed a real double-present regression in r430's fix; r433 catalogued (without committing) the wider native/ uncommitted backlog r432 discovered. r434 pursued the remaining open thread named since r431 -- the real visual content of presents, still a placeholder color clear -- and found a precise root cause, not just 'not yet done': PinnedShaderRuntime (native_vulkan_backend.cpp) is a complete, tested real-rendering engine (draw_pinned real indexed draws, EDRAM resolve, real texture sampling, built and verified end-to-end across r256-r270) but is referenced ONLY by native_xenos_tests.cpp -- never by native_runtime.cpp, native_guest_vd.cpp, or ac6recomp_main.cpp, i.e. never by the live VdSwap path, which calls only VulkanBackend::submit() (validates/counts, no rendering) and present_to_offscreen() (a plain color clear, comment already says 'placeholder until resolve-to-image lands'). Deeper than a missing call: PinnedShaderRuntime's shared-memory SSBO is a bounded 64 MiB buffer with DIRECT address-as-offset semantics (draw.vertex_address/index_address used verbatim as byte offset), sized and addressed for synthetic test addresses (0x1000, 0x2000...), not real 32-bit Xbox 360 guest addresses that can range across 512 MiB of physical RAM. Wiring execute_frame into the live path without first measuring real draw addresses would likely fail-closed on most real draws, or render wrong if an address mapping were guessed. Decision: do not wire this blind -- measure first. Named for r435: capture real DrawPacket guest addresses live via gdb (same technique as r426/r428/r429) on the actual retail drain/submit path, to determine whether the 64 MiB direct-offset window can work as-is or whether PinnedShaderRuntime's shared-memory contract needs a redesign (wider window and/or guest-address-to-SSBO-offset remapping) before any live wiring. No source file touched this cycle (read-only investigation); gates/ctest unaffected from r433's state. The wider native/ backlog commit decision (r433) remains open and untouched, unrelated to this finding.
